outcome: Give farm operations director / food quality head a governed method to improve soil health parameter variance using laboratory soil tests, crop rotation and fertilizer records, with final decisions…
overview: Soil Health Trend Monitoring addresses telemetry is noisy or missing, so operators spend time interpreting unrelated warnings in agriculture and food production operations. The first proof of value uses laboratory soil tests, crop rotation and fertilizer records. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is soil health parameter variance, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

benefits.limits: Basis: customer-specific hypothesis. No uplift promised; validate in controlled pilot

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: laboratory soil tests, crop rotation and fertilizer records; define soil health parameter variance and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Farm Operations Director / Food Quality Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including inject sensor failures, stale data and dependency loss into the pilot.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
